title: Local lifting of a module presentation of a finite constant quotient
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $\Lambda$ a finite ring, and $S$ a short exact sequence of sheaves of left $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Suppose $S_3$ is constant [def-constructible-constant] with finitely generated geometric stalks [def-constructible-finite]. There is an etale cover $(U_i\to X)_i$ such that for every $i$ there is a short exact sequence $T_i$ with finitely generated first term $(T_i)_1$ of $\Lambda$-modules, an isomorphism $e_i:\underline{(T_i)_3}\simeq S_3|_{U_i}$, and a map $r_i:\underline{(T_i)_2}\to S_2|_{U_i}$ with $(S.g|_{U_i})\circ r_i=e_i\circ\underline{T_i.g}$. There is no cokernel assertion and no constancy hypothesis on $S_1$.

source.place: Tag 093U, extension paragraph: finite free surjection onto N and simultaneous local lifts of its generators (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/093U)

proof.text: On an empty X use the empty cover. Otherwise choose a constant model N of S_3 and one geometric point. The constant-sheaf stalk is N: apply Point.sheafFiberConstantSheafIso from WeilConjectures.Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Sites.Point.ConstantSheaf. Transport finite generation from the given stalk to N using ModuleCat.isFinitelyGenerated_iff. This stalk computation works for left modules over a Ring, without commutativity.

Choose finitely many generators of N. The linear map from the free module P on this finite set to N is surjective. Its kernel K gives the short exact module complex T = (K -> P -> N). The finite ring and finite basis make P a finite set. Its kernel K is a finite set, hence is generated by its finite set of all elements, for arbitrary left modules over this ring.

The quotient map is epi. Use local surjectivity on each of the finitely many generator sections, as in lem-constructible-shortexact-local-lift, in the fixed-coefficient category Sheaf J (ModuleCat Lambda). The existing theorem uses SheafOfModules with commutative coefficients, so use instead the generic Mathlib Sheaf.isLocallySurjective_iff_epi' for ModuleCat and its forgetful functor. Refine the finitely many covers by fibre products to obtain simultaneous lifts. Their indices can be chosen small, since the etale site is essentially small.

By the universal property of the constant free sheaf, the lifted generators define r. Constant sheaves commute with etale pullback, giving e. The equality r followed by S.g = constant(T.g) followed by e holds on the free generators, hence as a morphism. This constructs precisely the displayed data.
